title: Ministerial statements on the Middle East conflict and support measures for Singapore
what_it_is: A series of ministerial statements addressing parliamentary questions on the impact of the Middle East situation on Singapore, followed by grouped clarifications from ministers.
why_it_matters: The statements set out support measures including $200 cash for active platform workers, private hire car drivers and taxi drivers from the end of the month; enhanced U-Save rebates; $500 CDC vouchers brought forward to June 2026; and a $200 increase to the Budget 2026 Cost-of-Living Special Payment, with about 2.4 million Singaporeans receiving cash in September. They also state that the regulated electricity tariff is expected to rise more sharply in the next adjustment and that overall inflation for 2026 is expected to be higher than earlier projected.

key_points.point: The conflict has entered its sixth week and Iran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, with vessel traffic falling sharply.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: Last month, only about six vessels on average passed through the Strait of Hormuz each day, compared to around 135 in normal times.

key_points.point: Brent crude oil prices doubled from just before the conflict to a peak.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: Since the onset of the conflict, Brent crude oil prices have doubled from US$71 per barrel just before the conflict, to a peak of US$141.

key_points.point: The Government convened the Homefront Crisis Ministerial Committee, chaired by Mr K Shanmugam.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: This is why we have convened the Homefront Crisis Ministerial Committee (HCMC), chaired by Coordinating Minister for National Security K Shanmugam and comprising several Ministers.

key_points.point: The regulated electricity tariff increased by 2.1% to about 27.27 cents per kWh for the second quarter of 2026.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: The regulated electricity tariff, which most Singapore households pay, increased by 2.1% to about 27.27 cents per kilowatt hour (kWh) for the second quarter of 2026.

key_points.point: Overall inflation for 2026 is now expected to be higher than earlier projected.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: Consequently, we now expect Singapore's overall inflation for 2026 to be higher than earlier projected.

key_points.point: MAS will release its upcoming assessment of the inflation outlook on 14 April 2026.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: MAS will take these developments into account in its upcoming assessment of the inflation outlook, which it will release on 14 April 2026.

key_points.point: Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese jointly affirmed commitment to support the flow of essential goods including diesel and LNG.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: They jointly affirmed our commitment to support the flow of essential goods, including petroleum oils, such as diesel, and LNG between our two countries.

key_points.point: Budget 2026 was presented on 12 February 2026 at $155 billion.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: On 12 February 2026, the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance presented our largest Budget on record, at $155 billion.

key_points.point: U-Save rebates were enhanced to 1.5 times the regular amount, or up to $570 this financial year.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: We also enhanced U-Save rebates, giving 1.5 times the regular amount – or up to $570 this financial year.

key_points.point: The Government will disburse $200 in cash to active platform workers, private hire car drivers and taxi drivers from the end of the month.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: the Government will disburse $200 in cash to active platform workers, private hire car drivers and taxi drivers from the end of the month.

key_points.point: For certain essential bus services, the Government will provide temporary assistance to co-fund cost increases.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: For certain essential bus services, such as those for school students, seniors and persons with disabilities, the Government will provide temporary assistance to co-fund cost increases, to enable these services to continue operating without disruption.

key_points.point: The Government does not think reducing fuel or diesel subsidies across the board is the right move.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: We do not think this is the right move. It is too blunt an approach and it could also be regressive.

key_points.point: Mr Jeffrey Siow clarified that he had misread and meant fuel or diesel duties, not subsidies.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: I earlier said that several Members have asked if the Government will consider reducing fuel or diesel subsidies. I misread. What I meant to say was that several Members have asked if the Government will consider reducing fuel or diesel duties.

key_points.point: The Corporate Income Tax rebate will be enhanced from 40% to 50% for the Year of Assessment 2026.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: we will enhance the Corporate Income Tax rebate announced at Budget from 40% to 50% for the Year of Assessment 2026.

key_points.point: The minimum benefit for a company with at least one local employee will be raised from $1,500 to $2,000.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: We will also raise the minimum benefit that a company with at least one local employee will receive, from $1,500 to $2,000.

key_points.point: The total benefits cap for each company will be raised from $30,000 to $40,000.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: The total benefits cap for each company will be raised from $30,000 to $40,000.

key_points.point: The base tier of the Energy Efficiency Grant will be expanded to all sectors and extended to 31 March 2028.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: We will now expand the base tier of this grant to all sectors and extend this support for another year, to 31 March 2028

key_points.point: The Government is prepared to share fuel-related cost increases for critical Government projects including the Cross Island MRT Line and new HDB BTO projects.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: This includes major Government infrastructure projects, such as the Cross Island Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) Line and new Housing and Development Board (HDB) Build-To-Order (BTO) projects.

key_points.point: The $500 CDC vouchers announced in Budget this year will be brought forward from January 2027 to June 2026.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: we will bring forward the disbursement of the $500 CDC vouchers announced in Budget this year from January 2027 to June 2026.

key_points.point: The Budget 2026 Cost-of-Living Special Payment will be increased by $200 for all eligible Singaporeans.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: We will also increase the Budget 2026 Cost-of-Living Special Payment by $200 for all eligible Singaporeans.

key_points.point: About 2.4 million Singaporeans will receive the additional payment in cash in September.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: About 2.4 million Singaporeans will receive this additional payment in cash, which will be disbursed in September.

key_points.point: The package adds up to close to $1 billion in additional measures on top of Budget 2026 commitments.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: This package adds up to close to $1 billion in additional measures, on top of what has previously been committed in Budget 2026.

key_points.point: The Government will work within the amount approved in the Supply Act last month first and seek Parliament's approval for a supplementary budget later.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: To fund these measures, the Government will work within the amount approved in the Supply Act last month in the first instance, and seek Parliament's approval for the supplementary budget later on.

key_points.point: The HCMC has 13 members whose names are in an Annex.
key_points.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
key_points.quote: There are 13 members in this HCMC and their names are in the Annex.

key_points.point: ICA increased checks at checkpoints and Police stepped up patrols at areas of concern.
key_points.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
key_points.quote: The Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) has increased checks at our checkpoints upon the escalation of the conflict, and Police have also stepped up patrols at areas of concern.

key_points.point: Contingency plans were activated to repatriate Singaporeans in the Middle East affected by the conflict.
key_points.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
key_points.quote: We also activated contingency plans to repatriate Singaporeans in the Middle East affected by the conflict.

key_points.point: More than half of Singapore's total crude oil imports come from the Middle East.
key_points.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
key_points.quote: More than half of our total crude oil imports comes from the Middle East.

key_points.point: Singapore has not imposed export restrictions on fuel or implemented fuel rationing, and so far there has been no need to do so.
key_points.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
key_points.quote: Since the start of the conflict, several countries have announced export restrictions on fuel or implemented fuel rationing measures. We have not done so. So far, there has been no need to do so.

key_points.point: Singapore has secured crude oil supplies from alternative sources but pays much higher prevailing prices.
key_points.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
key_points.quote: We have secured crude oil supplies from alternative sources. But we have to pay prevailing prices, which are much higher.

key_points.point: Singapore imports LNG from Australia, the US and Mozambique, apart from the Middle East.
key_points.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
key_points.quote: Apart from the Middle East, we also import LNG from Australia, one of our key suppliers; the US; and Mozambique.

key_points.point: Power plants can switch from natural gas to diesel when needed.
key_points.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
key_points.quote: Second, while 95% of our electricity is generated from natural gas, our power plants can switch from natural gas to diesel when needed.

key_points.point: The Government is planning to increase fuel reserves.
key_points.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
key_points.quote: We are also planning to increase our fuel reserves.

key_points.point: Singaporeans should be prepared for supplies of some foods from some countries to be unavailable and exercise flexibility in choosing alternatives.
key_points.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
key_points.quote: Singaporeans should be prepared for supplies of some foods from some countries to be unavailable and will have to exercise flexibility in choosing alternatives.

key_points.point: As a policy, the Government does not disclose the extent of fuel reserves and food stockpiles.
key_points.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
key_points.quote: As a policy, we do not disclose these.

key_points.point: Advanced nuclear energy technologies are being studied, with five uranium pellets one-inch-tall able to generate the same electricity as one Olympic-sized swimming pool of natural gas.
key_points.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
key_points.quote: Five uranium pellets one-inch-tall can generate the same amount of electricity as one Olympic-sized swimming pool of natural gas.

key_points.point: The Government announced at the March Committee of Supply debate that it would raise the solar target to three gigawatt-peak.
key_points.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
key_points.quote: At the Committee of Supply debate in March, the Government announced that it would raise the target to three gigawatt-peak.

key_points.point: There is no upstream disruption from piped natural gas supply at this point.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: At this particular point in time, there is no upstream disruption from the piped natural gas supply.

key_points.point: Quarterly audits show generation companies are 99.9% ready to switch to diesel.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: Thus far, our audit statistics have shown that we are 99.9% ready in switching.

key_points.point: There is no immediate risk to seafood supply.
key_points.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
key_points.quote: On seafood specifically, we do not see immediate risk.

key_points.point: Singapore has awarded conditional approval or conditional licensing of up to about 8.35 gigawatts of renewable energy, exceeding the original six gigawatt target.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: we have already awarded both conditional approval or conditional licensing of up to about 8.35 gigawatts of renewable energy. Our original target was six gigawatts – we have exceeded that.

key_points.point: Singapore can be a fast adopter but cannot be the first-of-a-kind mover for nuclear technology.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: We can be a fast adopter, but we cannot be the first-of-a-kind mover.

key_points.point: Diesel prices have risen mainly due to global factors.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: Our diesel prices have risen mainly due to global factors.

key_points.point: MRI operations will not be affected for now by helium supply issues.
key_points.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
key_points.quote: So, MRI operations will not be affected for now.

key_points.point: Wafer fabs here have a multi-source strategy for helium supplies.
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: By and large, the wafer fabs here have a multi-source strategy for helium supplies.

key_points.point: The Government does not dictate petrol prices or price changes so long as prices are set independently.
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: The Government does not dictate the prices or price changes of businesses, so long as the prices are set independently.

key_points.point: MPA will assess whether port services are critical and make a case to MOF for support.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: the Maritime Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) will assess that and make a case to the Ministry of Finance (MOF) for support.

key_points.point: The Government runs simulations across chronological and geographical parameters.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: We simulate models across chronological parameters as well as geographical parameters.

key_points.point: MOE is monitoring utility costs for school canteen stallholders.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: On the question for MOE on canteen stallholders, we are monitoring the utility costs for them.

key_points.point: The $200 for private hire car drivers is currently a one-off, and the Government will watch how things develop.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: on private hire car drivers, the $200 is currently a one-off, but we will watch how things develop and if there is a need for us to do more, we can come in again.

key_points.point: During COVID-19, HDB provided additional assistance such as rental waivers for HDB rental shops.
key_points.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
key_points.quote: during COVID-19, HDB had provided additional assistance, such as rental waivers for HDB rental shops.

key_points.point: The crisis is temporary in a sense, but its impact will be quite long lasting.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: I think this crisis is temporary – in a sense, and all crises are temporary, But I think the impact of this crisis will be quite long lasting.

key_points.point: The Government is watching the risk of misinformation and disinformation that could threaten social cohesion.
key_points.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
key_points.quote: That is the risk of misinformation and disinformation that could threaten our social cohesion

key_points.point: Singapore's position is that there is a right of transit passage through straits used for international navigation, not a toll to be paid.
key_points.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
key_points.quote: There is a right of transit passage. It is not a privilege to be granted by the bordering state. It is not a licence to be supplicated for. It is not a toll to be paid.

key_points.point: Singapore cannot engage in negotiations for safe passage of ships or negotiate on toll rates.
key_points.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
key_points.quote: I cannot engage in negotiations for safe passage of ships or negotiate on toll rates.

key_points.point: There are legal provisions enshrined regarding gas supply.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: Today, there are legal provisions that are enshrined.

key_points.point: Singapore has contingency plans for a disruption to the Strait of Malacca.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: The answer is yes.

what_happens_next: MAS will release its inflation outlook on 14 April 2026; MTI will update the GDP forecast in May; BCA will issue a circular shortly; the Government will seek Parliament's approval for a supplementary budget later; the HCMC will continue to monitor the situation. The Sitting was suspended until 5.30 pm.
not_said: What will be the exact size and timing of the supplementary budget?
Will the announced support measures be extended beyond the current one-off payments?
How long would Singapore's fuel reserves and food stockpiles last under different disruption scenarios?
Will any partner countries impose export restrictions on energy supplies to Singapore?
When will the Strait of Hormuz reopen and when will the conflict end?
Will inflation pass-through continue into 2027 and 2028?
Which additional sectors, if any, will receive targeted support?
What specific measures are included in the contingency plans for a Strait of Malacca disruption?
How will the Government assess and respond to profiteering in essential food items?
